steps.message:
# Ship is damaged when performing the action shown in the recording

### What happens
`recording.mp4` shows a ship performing an action at a station. The action does not
go the way it is set up to go, and the ship does not come out of it unharmed.
The ship takes damage from the very start of the action shown in the video, before it visibly hits anything. Both the ship's and the station's models are involved. Nothing else about the ships or stations should change.

### Expected
Performing the action shown in the recording must not damage the ship at all, at the spot shown in
the video or at any other equivalent spot of the same station. The hull-integrity readout stays at
100% for the whole action.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4`

You can inspect the video frame by frame with `ffmpeg` (installed in the image), e.g. extracting
still frames at specific timestamps to look closely at the HUD and the ship.

Inspect the attached file before making changes. The video describes observable behavior; it does
not prescribe source files, internal names, or an implementation strategy.

        idx=[int(x) for x in tp.find(ns+'p').text.split()][off::stride]

        if vc is not None:
            k=0

steps.message:
I've changed two station model files so that a ship taking off from a pad no longer starts out buried in the pad's collision surface. I couldn't check this in the game: SDL isn't installed and no game binary is built, so the fix is based on reading the model geometry, not on watching the hull readout.

**What the video shows:** a Coronatrix (the Mars start ship) taking off from Cydonia with fixed-speed takeoff. Hull integrity drops from 100% to 99% the moment the thrusters fire, before the ship touches anything you can see. The station seed shows Cydonia uses the `new_ground` station model.

**Cause:** a docked ship is placed so its lowest point sits exactly on the pad's landing tag. The Coronatrix's collision mesh reaches exactly down to that tag, as most ships' meshes do, so the pad's collision surface must not sit above it. On `new_ground` it did:
- **Pad 1** was 0.73 m above its landing tag, raised 0.47 m more than the other pads even though all six share the same mesh.
- **Pads 2–6** were 0.26 m above their tags.

When takeoff starts, the ship switches back to normal flight while partly inside the pad slab. The station no longer counts the pad as part of a docking, so every contact with it goes to the station's ship-damage handler. Contacts whose normal points against the climbing ship count as an impact, and that is where the damage at the very start comes from.

**Fix (data only, no code changes):**
- `data/models/stations/new_ground/new_ground_landing.dae`: all six collision pads are now at z = 72.58245, level with their landing tags and with the centre of the visible pad. The station's other collision geometry is at least 60 m from each pad centre, so nothing else overlaps a landed ship.
- `data/models/stations/ground_station/starport_docking.dae`: I found the same fault on the other surface station. Pads 9 and 13 share a collision mesh whose top was 9.4 cm above their tags, so I made them flush at z = 40 like the other 12 pads. That station isn't the one in the video; this part is a judgement call and easy to revert if you don't want it.

Nothing else in the station or ship models changed. Ships now touch down about 0.26 m lower on `new_ground` pads, which is the height of the visible pad's centre. Because the pads were raised by a constant amount and the ship meshes reach their tags, this should hold at every pad and for other ships. The test that would confirm it is to launch the Coronatrix from each Cydonia pad and watch the hull readout stay at 100%.
